question: Can a data-dependent cumulative pre-softmax decay provide a distinct attention-routing intervention within the existing10M budget?

literature.evidence_scope: Primary paper uses substantially larger models and other data/context; not Japanese10M quality evidence or a diagnosis of the current failure.

mechanism.attention: softmax(original scaled QK^T+d, causal valid keys)*original V
mechanism.padding: Invalid physical slots contribute0 to cumulative log gate and cannot be attended; no batch-row crossover
mechanism.cache: Full and chunked paths must use the same concatenated valid-token log-gate history; no implicit native KVCache compatibility
mechanism.original_components: Keep original GQA Q4/KV2, NoQKNorm, RoPE, SwiGLU and frozen native sources; no Pro output gate, QK norm, KV shift, ACP or RoPE removal.

novelty: Actual old output gate multiplies an already-normalized head output and doubles O at conversion. This proposed pairwise pre-softmax decay changes normalized key ratios; not the same operation. Old causal-QKV adds preceding raw features, old first-V transfers layer values, and cross-map subtracts another GQA map. Registered source searches and direct source inspection only, not proof of all historical work or quality.

declined_routes.next_two: Actual original proposal/trainer/config/completion show next-two auxiliary learning already rejected; head/horizon/coefficient rescue forbidden. Historical train-only688896 also exceeds current total-training10M budget and is not a precedent for new over-budget heads.
declined_routes.recurrent: Existing novelty review declined full-stack recurrence as reopening closed sharing; no visit-order/gate/residual rescue.
